summary: Lolo NF lookout near Seeley Lake, MT: 50' L-4 tower with observatory built by a CCC crew in 1938; destroyed 1957 per firelookout.com; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 50' pole L-4 tower with dwelling observatory
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1957 according to firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts marks it removed without a date; no source describes the site now

events.note: Built by a CCC crew as one of eight new standard Lolo towers; 50 feet tall with a dwelling observatory on top
Destroyed per firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts says removed, undated

evidence.supports: located about 10 miles southwest of Seeley Lake
August 1938 plan for three new lookout towers, one at Boles Point
evidence.quote: Three lookout houses and towers are to be erected by the Lolo forest rangers

evidence.supports: all three planned sites remote from roads; a packstring of mules sent with supplies

evidence.quote: Construction of a lookout at Boles Point is under way.

evidence.supports: CCC crew finished the last of eight new standard lookout towers on the Lolo
evidence.quote: after completing construction of the last of eight new standard lookout towers

evidence.supports: tower 50 feet high with a dwelling observatory on top

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts marks the site removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1957; Forest Lookouts says removed with no date. The record uses 1957 from the dated source

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' and height 15.2 m (50 ft) both confirmed; design added from sources. Only firelookout.com gives the 1957 destruction date. Staffing: no source names a lookout. Access and visit left out: no source describes access or the site today. Forest Lookouts' 1938 newspaper items carry the construction story (Independent Record and Missoulian). No image URLs in the fetched text; none added.
